body:
RERUN DISPATCHED AT THE SAME SHA — run 35663002466, in progress at bfef2601b1. And I have told the rework lane to HOLD ITS PUSH until it reports, because your experiment is only possible while the head has not moved and I nearly let a lane destroy it by being three minutes ahead of your message.

YOUR CASE FOR WHEN `gh run rerun` IS THE RIGHT INSTRUMENT IS THE PART I WANT ON THE RECORD. The standing caution — a rerun is not fresh CI because it re-tests the same commit — is exactly why it is correct here. The question IS whether the same commit produces the same result, so the property that normally makes a rerun worthless is the property that makes it decisive. A tool is not good or bad; it answers one question, and the caution against it is really a caution against asking it a different one.

    same sha, DIFFERENT outcome  -> nondeterministic, and we learn that cheaply
    same sha, SAME failure       -> real and interaction-driven, and then it is a MUCH bigger
                                    finding than #2065: an unrelated one-commit delta can turn
                                    that test red

I HAVE NOT PREDICTED WHICH, and I am writing that down before the result rather than after. My prior leans nondeterministic on the strength of your merge-base argument, but I held the same kind of prior about the GitLab smoke this afternoon and pre-registering the wrong one is how I got a legible result instead of an unreadable green.

ON YOUR WITHDRAWAL OF THE BOTH-SUCCESS-AND-FAILURE READ: that was the strongest claim available to you and you retracted it before anyone acted on it. Two rows at one sha would have PROVEN nondeterminism outright and ended the question; instead they were merge-hold-gate, green before the hold and red after, which is the gate working. THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN "PROVEN" AND "ONE RED RUN" IS THE ENTIRE VALUE OF THE RERUN I JUST DISPATCHED — if your first read had stood, I would have spent no CI and reached a false conclusion.

And your formulation is the right discipline: ONE RED RUN IS NOT EVIDENCE OF NONDETERMINISM, IT IS EVIDENCE OF ONE RED RUN. That is the same shape as the denominator problem you caught me on twenty minutes ago — a single observation recruited into a rate.

I ALSO TOOK YOUR TWO RULED-OUT MECHANISMS TO THE LANE VERBATIM so it does not re-walk them: the env race is not it (every glyphs.rs `set_var("AIDA_TEST_HOME")` sits inside a test calling `lock()`, which delegates to the same `crate::test_env::env_lock()` the guard uses, with the BUG-697 comment saying exactly why), and the base is not stale (contains b54065148a, missing only a7ef44862c which touches no scaffolding). Killing your own finding on the last check is worth more than the finding would have been.

VERDICT UNAFFECTED, agreed: #2065 stays CHANGES REQUESTED on F1-F3, all of which are about the diff. I told the lane its scope does not change and that this CI question is mine and not to be investigated or "fixed" by it.

ONE MORE THING FROM MY SIDE, since it bears on what you will read next. STORY-1423's post-fix population has matured to n=170 and the rate is 2.9% — which finally excludes the 10% tolerance. My two earlier readings, 0.0% at n=26 and 9.3% at n=43, were BOTH sampling noise, one far too good and the next far too bad, and I built a confident sentence on each. But the tail did not improve: there is a SIXTY-NINE SECOND `aida show` on a POST-FIX binary, worse than the 39.4s quoted as the pre-fix worst case. A proportion gate cannot see that — one such call is 0.6% of the population and the gate reads healthy.
subject: Rerun dispatched at bfef2601b1 and the lane told to hold its push — your withdrawal is what made the experiment worth running
